notes: All four tools are included unconditionally in the server's `tools` array (`dist/index.js:13-17`) and advertised by iterating that array (`dist/index.js:34-46`), so they are default-enabled.

Every tool invocation queues anonymous telemetry for the tool name (`dist/index.js:55-65`), and README documents opt-out with `NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1` (`README.md:244-260`); no advertised tool is removed by that setting.

browser_eval.rationale: `browser_eval` executes fixed local probe commands with `execSync` to determine whether `agent-browser` is installed and to read `agent-browser --version`, then returns the local installation status and version. This is host-local, non-public environment information, so it is SECRET. The command strings are fixed and do not include agent-supplied input, so this is not arbitrary HOSTEXEC.

nextjs_call.rationale: `nextjs_call` forwards the selected `toolName` and `args` to a local Next.js runtime MCP endpoint via `callNextJsTool` and returns the runtime `result`. The documented runtime tools can expose errors, logs, route/project metadata, and server-action source-file resolution, which are non-public local application/runtime data, so it is SECRET. Because the returned `result` is opaque output from runtime tools such as browser/server logs and errors, it may include text originating outside the MCP server; the internal runtime manager and exact Next.js tool behavior are not included, so UNTRUSTED is kept with `undetermined` true. The tool can also invoke runtime tools that change application state, e.g. the description lists cache management, so its kind is WRITE.

nextjs_docs.rationale: `nextjs_docs` reads local project files under `project_path`, including `node_modules/next/package.json` and `package.json`, and returns local Next.js version/source information, docs availability, paths, and instructions containing local paths. This exposes non-public host filesystem/project metadata, so it is SECRET.

nextjs_index.rationale: `nextjs_index` discovers/probes local Next.js dev servers and returns local server metadata such as `port`, `pid`, `command`, `url`, and available runtime MCP tool names/schemas. That is non-public local host/application state, so it is SECRET. The exact discovery/probing implementation is imported from `../_internal/nextjs-runtime-manager.js`, which was not provided, so the precise reach is undetermined.
